newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares weighed down by Primofin.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares weighed down by Primofin.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 1.12 percent on Thursday and traders said they could continue falling tomorrow on expectations of bad earnings from financial consultancy Primofin.
Primofin said it would announce its revised 1995 results on Friday or Saturday.
"Apparently the market believes Primofin's results will be worse than expected. That is why its shares fell substantially and pulled others down too," one trader said.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 11.06 points to 973,59.
* Seven shares fell and five rose, while 11 were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 103.7 million tolars from 50.4 million.
* Primofin had the highest turnover and was the leading decliner, tumbling 26.77 percent to 25,632 tolars on volume of 2,190 shares for total turnover of 56.1 million tolars.
* Trading company Kovinotehna was the biggest gainer, rising 1.09 percent to 430 on volume of 407 shares for total turnover of 0.2 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
